tests.mutation: In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountCreatureStatement.NamedByTheCorpus named only the mule (`Kind == MountCreatureKind.Mule`), so a domesticated horse declined; this test went red, and so did controlled-mount-turn's.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountRules.Control declined only where the caller stated the creature was not trained (`if (creature.Training == MountTraining.NotTrained)`), so an unstated training was read as untrained; this test went red, and so did controlled-mount-turn's decline and both of the tests for a stated training.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; MountRules.Control ignored the caller's stated training and declined for every creature the corpus does not name (`if (creature.Training != MountTraining.FromTheCorpus)`), which is version 6's behaviour; this test went red, and so did controlled-mount-turn's carrying of the ruling.

rulings.span: Which creatures have been trained to accept a rider? The corpus gives instances (“Domesticated horses, mules, and similar creatures”) and no definition, and “similar” states no measure. For a creature not named, nothing in the slice says whether it is trained or who decides.
rulings.answer: The caller states it: training to accept a rider is a fact the caller supplies, and the horse and the mule the corpus names are trained without being told.
